across: Paired by task, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are within noise on single days (v2, v3) and Sol is clearly ahead on 3-day weather fronts (v4: +23.1 pts of hindsight capture, 95% CI [9.0, 48.0]). The untrained Qwen3-4B has the lowest capture throughout.

bench.pitch: Fifteen models in native agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode for the open Beam-⁠1.0, GLM-⁠5.3, GLM-⁠5.3-⁠Flash, Kimi K3, Qwen3.8 Max, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen3.5-⁠9B, Qwen3.5-⁠9B + desk SFT and Qwen3-⁠4B) run a real ERCOT battery's trading desk for three days at a time across 8 real Texas weather fronts, graded in dollars against the hindsight optimum and the battery's real operator.
bench.framework: 0.9.1377 (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna), 0.9.1378 (Qwen3-4B), 0.9.1383 (Gemini 4 Argon) and 0.9.1396 (Beam-1.0, GLM-5.3, Kimi K3, Qwen3.8 Max, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT, Claude Haiku 5.5, GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GPT-6.1 Terra)

anchor.label: The anchor, the desk's own optimiser

lead.head: GPT-6.1 Sol captures the most of hindsight:
lead.text: C 27.0% [9.5, 43.8] over its 32 windows, at $4.12 a window. Paired by window, its lead over DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: +2.5 pts [−8.2, +12.8], a CI that includes zero.

operator.head: Against the real operator:
operator.text: its own bids, replayed through the same clearing and settlement, capture 7.4%. Ahead of them paired by window, with a CI above zero: GPT-6.1 Sol, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GPT-6.1 Terra, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3-Flash, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5. Behind, with a CI below zero: Qwen3-4B.

frontier.head: Cost against score:
frontier.text: The cost frontier, cheapest first: GLM-5.3-Flash ($0.15, C 16.9%), DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ($0.38, C 24.6%) and GPT-6.1 Sol ($4.12, C 27.0%). No other model is both cheaper and higher in C; the other 12 are dominated.

sft.head: Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT reproduces the desk's own planner.
sft.text: It is a LoRA SFT of Qwen3.5-9B with TRL, through AgentEnv, on OpenCode transcripts of the desk's own planner, the anchor policy, which calls optimize and submits its proposal; it reproduces the planner, not trading it learned on its own. The planner captures 20.9% on these windows and Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT 20.3%; over base Qwen3.5-9B, served differently, +13.0 pts [+6.3, +19.6], the desk-distill pre-registration's secondary comparison; on its primary test, 18 held-out windows, it missed the pre-registered bar, +3.8 pts [−3.4, +10.6] over base.

text.halves: Every model scores lower on Jul–Aug than on Jan–May, and that includes Qwen3-4B, whose training predates every window. So the drop reflects harder windows (the Jan–May half includes winter storm Fern), not evidence of training-data contamination. No model the rule covers has a post − pre interval that excludes zero, so all 32 windows lead, by a rule set before any API result.
text.reliability: 621 attempts for 480 model-windows; 145 did not reach the grade (infrastructure ×141, episode spend cap, final ×4). Infrastructure failures were retried; attempts that failed before any model call (a port race in our launcher, $0), Gemini 4 Argon's ended by a transient provider 400 from 18:06 UTC and Beam-1.0's ended by the router's HTTP 402 when its account ran out of credits didn't count toward the two-retry limit (see Deviations). Windows not scored and not imputed: Kimi K3, episode spend cap, final ×4.
text.rule: The pre-registered rule that the post-cutoff half leads if the halves differ guards against training-data contamination, so, as read before any API-model result, only a model whose reported training cutoff comes after the first pre-cutoff window (GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon, GPT-6.1 Terra, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Beam-1.0) can trigger it, when its post − pre interval in C excludes zero; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT, GLM-5.3, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8 Max and Qwen3.5-9B, with no reported cutoff, can trigger it too.

harness.head: Each model in a native agent harness,
harness.text: through AgentEnv: GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna in Codex CLI 0.147.0 with OpenAI's catalog entries for the GPT-6 models; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT, GLM-5.3, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8 Max, Qwen3.5-9B, Beam-1.0 and Qwen3-4B in OpenCode 1.17.18; Gemini 4 Argon in Gemini CLI 0.38.2; GPT-6.1 Terra in Codex CLI 0.147.0 with OpenAI's catalog entries for the GPT-6 models and one for Terra copied from Sol's; Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 in Claude Code 2.1.280. The open-weight models: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Z.ai's GLM-5.3, Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, Z.ai's GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8 Max and Qwen3.5-9B, served by Fireworks; Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT, served by vLLM 0.29.0 on EC2 GPU boxes (g7e.8xlarge); Reflection's Beam-1.0, served by Baseten through the Hugging Face router; Qwen3-4B, served by vLLM 0.29.0 on EC2 GPU boxes (g5.2xlarge, g5.xlarge).

internet.head: No internet.
internet.text: Each run's Docker network is closed to the internet by a host rule, and the model is reached only through a proxy on the host that allows one API and one model per run and refuses provider-side web, code-execution and remote-MCP tools; the agents hold only a placeholder key, which the proxy replaces. Web search and fetch are also off in each harness's own settings; checked from inside the agent containers before the runs.

tools.head: The desk's 11 tools over MCP,
tools.text: beside the harness's own shell, files and planning tools; v4's budget of 100 turns, 14 desk calls a turn and 12 reminders. One run per model per window.

l0.head: The env's control endpoints are not authenticated
l0.text: in this framework release, and an agent's shell can reach the env through its tunnel; no pilot showed an attempt to use them, and the runs are not audited for it.

l1.head: Model plus harness.
l1.text: Each harness's own prompts, tools and context handling are part of what is measured; the harness versions are the ones the framework release pins. Gemini CLI drops a thought signature when it resumes a session, which costs it prompt-cache hits and raises its cost, a known harness issue.

l2.head: The training cutoffs are third-party reports, unconfirmed.
l2.text: None is reported for GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash, Kimi K3, Qwen3.8 Max, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT, reportedly released 2 Mar–10 Sep 2026, so no front certainly post-dates all seven. The pre-cutoff half reuses v4's 16 windows, which GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and Qwen3-4B also played on the desk's own runner (below).

l3.head: One run per model per window over eight fronts,
l3.text: so the CIs are wide, and a single scarcity front can carry a model's dollars.

l4.head: Cost is the model maker's list price:
l4.text: tokens at each maker's public price per million, without batch or volume discounts; a maker's higher rate for a long prompt applies call by call, Claude Haiku 5.5's above 100K tokens to 1,101 of its calls; Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT and Qwen3-4B's cost is its share of the GPU time. Beam-1.0: Reflection publishes no price; at Together AI's list price including its $0.04 cached-read rate. Qwen3.5-9B: no maker price; at the metered Fireworks rate, $0.20 per 1M tokens, cached reads included.

l5.head: Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT are served differently:
l5.text: Qwen3.5-9B by Fireworks, Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT by our own vLLM 0.29.0 on EC2 GPU boxes (g7e.8xlarge), so numerics, the tool-call parser and sampling can differ between them.

l6.head: Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT's training data and these windows.
l6.text: Its training windows read D-7 to D2 of their dates, and only the 2026-05-08 front's operating days (05-08 to 05-10, its four windows) fall inside any of those spans, as the DAM and MCPC price history of the 16 training windows that start 2026-05-14 to 05-17. The training transcripts never name those days, and on those four windows its C is within 1.7 points of the planner's. The training pack, `data/desk/desk-v4-win`, is on the plugin's `desk-distill` branch at 13d53f9 and can be rebuilt with `scripts/desk_data_build.py` ([the check](https://github.com/earakely-scale/agentenv-gridsim-plugin/blob/desk-v4-bench-results-7/docs/prereg/desk-distill.md#after-the-results)).

l7.head: A known env defect, K1, in the benchmark too.
l7.text: An empty reserve-offer list drew a spurious ASO-02 note while the energy curves in the same call were accepted and applied; there is no settlement effect. It is fixed on the head; the frozen runs keep it, and the benchmark plays v4's freeze.

route.head: Route C
route.text: the episodes ran on EC2 boxes with local Docker rather than in Modal sandboxes; the internet was closed by a host rule and a per-run model proxy instead of Modal's network policy (the pre-registration gives the reasons).

errors.head: Provider HTTP 400s
errors.text: 19 of Gemini 4 Argon's 1,488 wake starts (1.28%) drew HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT, all on a wake's first request from turn 12 on and more often at larger prompts; the identical request succeeded on replay, so they are transient and infrastructure under the pre-registered rule, and were retried. From 18:06 UTC they did not count toward the two-retry limit, with a safety stop at 6 attempts a window; no window used more than 4.

credits.head: Out of credits
credits.text: the Hugging Face account ran out of prepaid credits at 01:55 UTC on 2026-10-31, after 29 of Beam-1.0's windows had been graded. The router's HTTP 402 then ended four attempts on the 2026-08-26 front, two mid-episode and two before any call; they were reclassified by hand as infrastructure, none counting toward the retry limit, and all four windows were graded once credits were added (the four 2026-08-26 windows all score below zero, S01 included, which ran before the halt).

limit.head: Output limit, decided during the runs
limit.text: from 07:39 UTC on 2026-10-31 an OpenCode call that ends at its 32,000-token output limit with no content or tool call, which makes the harness exit, counts as infrastructure toward the two-retry limit. It ended 11 GLM-5.3 attempts on 8 windows, 1 Kimi K3 attempt and 3 Qwen3.8 Max attempts on 2 windows; no window used its three attempts on it. C on the windows graded after a retry against those graded at once: GLM-5.3 10.9% (9) against 21.3% (23), Kimi K3 82.1% (1) against 14.8% (27), Qwen3.8 Max 17.4% (2) against 13.6% (30).

capped.head: Window cap
capped.text: Kimi K3's 2026-03-16 S04, 2026-05-08 S04, 2026-07-23 S04 and 2026-08-26 S01 stopped at the pre-registered $20 window cap after 34 to 60 turns and 396 to 449 model calls, as it polled the desk tools over a long cached context; they are final and unscored, never imputed, so Kimi K3's C is over its other 28 windows.

basis.head: Cost basis, decided after every run (2026-11-01)
basis.text: a model's cost is its tokens at its maker's list price, which every price here already was but Beam-1.0's. Reflection publishes no price for Beam-1.0 (its API is a free beta); it was costed at the Hugging Face router's $0.40 / $1.20 per million input / output tokens with cached input at the full input price, an upper bound of $1.97 a window, and the router's actual bill to Baseten for the run was about $32. It is now at Together AI's list price, $0.40 / $0.04 / $1.20 per million input / cached input / output tokens: $0.31 a window, one figure everywhere.

harness9b.head: Both Qwen3.5-9B harnesses differ from Qwen3-4B's
harness9b.text: a 262k-token context (262,144 for the SFT, 262,143 for base, the Fireworks deployment's maximum) where Qwen3-4B's had 32,768, and a cap of 20 OpenCode steps a turn where it had none; the output limit is 8,192 tokens for all three. That output limit ended 4 attempts of base Qwen3.5-9B and 1 of the SFT, each retried as infrastructure.

dsflash.head: Claude Haiku 5.5, GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
dsflash.text: added after the others at Edgar's request, for more models between $0.2 and $0.5 a window, by the pre-registration's items 52 to 55, committed before their first scored call, and run at once on 2026-11-01 from 16:02 to 17:16 UTC by route C on agentenv-framework 0.9.1396: Claude Haiku 5.5 in Claude Code 2.1.280 as Claude Opus 5.5's row, GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash served by Fireworks in OpenCode 1.17.18 as GLM-5.3's row. Each is costed at its maker's list price per million input / cached / output tokens: Claude Haiku 5.5 $0.10 / $0.01 / $0.50 with cache writes at $0.125, and $0.50 / $0.05 / $2.50 with writes at $0.625 on each call whose whole prompt passed 100K tokens, 1,101 of its calls; GLM-5.3-Flash $0.15 / $0.03 / $0.50; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $0.30 / $0.006 / $1.20, its peak rate throughout. Claude Haiku 5.5 and GLM-5.3-Flash graded every window on the first attempt; OpenCode's 32,768-token output limit ended two DeepSeek V4.1 Flash attempts, which were retried as infrastructure and graded on the second.

qwen9bsft.head: Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT
qwen9bsft.text: added after the others as the secondary comparison of the desk-distill pre-registration (docs/prereg/desk-distill.md); on that pre-registration's primary test, 18 held-out windows, it missed the bar (+3.8 points [−3.4, +10.6] over base). Served by our own vLLM 0.29.0 on two g7e.8xlarge boxes, not by Fireworks as base Qwen3.5-9B was, so the two 9B rows are served differently; it ran from 03:51 to 06:31 UTC on 2026-11-01, and its cost is GPU time at the $4.50 an hour spot price paid, $0.56 a window.

argon.head: Gemini 4 Argon
argon.text: first deferred for cost, it ran on 2026-10-29 from 16:41 to 19:45 UTC, after the others, by route C on its own box, on agentenv-framework 0.9.1383, whose Gemini harness no longer names its system-prompt file anew each turn (before, every turn start missed the prompt cache).

glm.text: added after the others to compare with Beam-1.0, by a selection rule stated before any result (the pre-registration's item 28), and run after them, from 07:17 to 16:24 UTC on 2026-10-31, served by Fireworks at its list prices per million input / cached input / output tokens (GLM-5.3 $1.40 / $0.26 / $4.40, Kimi K3 $3.00 / $0.30 / $15.00, Qwen3.8 Max $2.00 / $0.25 / $6.00), in OpenCode 1.17.18 at effort high like Beam-1.0, on agentenv-framework 0.9.1396, by route C on Beam-1.0's box; none of the three reports a training cutoff.

It is costed at OpenAI's list price per million input / cached / output tokens, $1.00 / $0.05 / $5.00 with cache writes at $1.25, and $2.00 / $0.10 / $7.50 with writes at $2.50 above a 272K-token prompt, which no call reached. The provider's token rate limit ended six attempts after Codex's own retries; they count as infrastructure and were retried, and each of those windows was graded on its second attempt.

qwen9b.head: Qwen3.5-9B
qwen9b.text: added after the others (the pre-registration's items 40 to 46) and run from 23:55 UTC on 2026-10-31 to 01:20 UTC on 2026-11-01 through a Fireworks dedicated deployment, in OpenCode 1.17.18 with thinking on, by route C. It has no maker price: Alibaba sells Qwen3.5 by the token only from 27B up and Qwen3.5-9B only as fine-tuning and dedicated deployment by the hour. So its cost is the metered Fireworks rate, $0.20 per million tokens with cached reads included: $3.20 a window.

cap.splits: C × 100: the share of the hindsight optimum's profit over idle that each model captured, its mean over the windows it finished on each side of the models' reported training cutoffs, Jan–May 2026 (may be in training data) and Jul–Aug 2026 (after every reported cutoff); none is reported for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT, GLM-5.3, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8 Max and Qwen3.5-9B; 95% CIs, a block bootstrap over the 8 fronts, are in the table below. Grey dashed: the real operator's own bids, replayed through the same clearing and settlement.

table.before: C, hindsight capture, %. Brackets: 95% CIs, a block bootstrap over the 8 weather fronts (four within each side of the cutoffs). cap.pareto: Each point is a model's mean C over its scored windows against its mean cost a window, on a log scale: the model maker's list price for its tokens, or GPU time for Qwen3.5-9B + desk SFT and Qwen3-4B. The step line is the cost frontier, the models no other model beats on both; the chart's notes give each cost's basis and what the distilled model is.
